name: Manganic-Architrave
description: Dust finer than flour pools in the low places, swallowing craters to their rims. Nothing has disturbed orbital debris ring in a million years, and the dust keeps its surface smooth as held breath.
Storm season reorganizes all plans. When the pressure falls, animals go quiet, instruments drift, and the horizon turns the color of an old wound.
Local legend among spacers says the planet hums on a frequency just below hearing. Instruments confirm it. Nobody agrees on the source.
There is money in uranium and platinum and history in the rocks, and the two keep interfering with each other. Mediators do brisk business at inflated rates.
